intro.en: How a child with belly complaints is examined, from the mouth and belly inspection to liver, spleen, fluid and gut sounds.

title.en: Mouth and throat check before the belly

items.summary: A quick tour of lips, gums, teeth, tongue, lining, tonsils and throat, which often explains belly complaints in a child.

blocks.title: What to note
bullets: Look at the lips for corner cracks, fissures, blisters and dark spots.
Look at the gums for swelling, bleeding and overgrowth, and note how clean the mouth is.
Count milk and adult teeth and note stains and decay.
Look at the tongue for dryness, a pale underside, yellow top or underside, blue tinge, thrush patches and surface bumps.
Look at the lining for ulcers, bleeding and dark spots that hint at polyp syndromes or adrenal disease.
Note whether the tonsils and throat look normal, large or inflamed.

viva.q: Why look at the tongue in a belly case?
viva.a: Paleness, yellowness, blueness and thrush point to anaemia, jaundice, low oxygen and thrush.

viva.q: What do dark spots inside the mouth suggest?
viva.a: They can hint at polyp syndromes or adrenal gland disease.

items.summary: Studying the shape, movement and surface of the belly from the foot end, plus the outward signs of liver failure.

blocks.title: Shape and surface
bullets: Note whether the belly looks flat and boat shaped or swollen, and whether the flanks look full.
Watch that all four quarters rise together with each breath.
Note whether the navel sits central and tucked in, or has shifted or pushed out.
Note whether the skin looks normal, stretched or glossy.
Look for throbs, scars, discharging openings, full veins, lumps and wave like gut movement.
Check the groin openings and look at the private parts.

blocks.title: Outward signs of liver failure
bullets: Look for yellow eyes, leg swelling and a fluid filled belly.
Look for red palms, tiny face vessels and swollen saliva glands.
Look for small testes and breast growth in boys.

viva.q: What does a shifted or pushed out navel mean?
viva.a: It points to fluid, a lump or pressure pulling the belly wall aside.

viva.q: Name four outward signs of liver failure.
viva.a: Yellow eyes, red palms, tiny face vessels and a swollen fluid filled belly.

viva.q: Why watch the belly move with breathing?
viva.a: A quarter that lags behind points to soreness, guarding or a lump beneath.

title.en: Feeling the belly, liver and spleen

items.summary: Gentle feeling for soreness and guarding, then the liver and spleen edge by edge, with the book's size guides and examples.

blocks.title: How to feel
bullets: Bend the hip and knee and ask for slow deep breaths so the wall relaxes.
Note warm skin over any patch of the belly.
Map sore spots, then judge soft versus guarding versus a board like wall.
Test release pain by lifting the hand briskly off a sore spot.

blocks.title: Liver
bullets: Feel below the right rib edge along the nipple line, sweeping toward the right groin.
Judge the edge as round or sharp and the face as smooth or bumpy.
Judge the feel as soft, firm or hard, and sore or painless.
Check it slides with breathing and that a finger cannot slip between lump and ribs.

head: Degree
Below rib edge
Book example
rows: Chronic myeloid leukaemia or liver cancer

blocks.title: Spleen
bullets: Feel below the left rib edge along the nipple line, sweeping down toward the navel line.
Judge the edge for its notch and the face as smooth or bumpy.
Judge the feel as soft, firm or hard, and sore or painless.
Check it slides with breathing, that fingers cannot pass above it, and whether the notch is felt.

head: Degree
Below rib edge
Book example
rows: Chronic myeloid leukaemia or kala azar

blocks.title: Finish
bullets: Feel for kidney, bladder and gland lumps that are not liver or spleen.
Skip the rectal check in children, as the book directs.
Confirm that both testes can be felt.

viva.q: How do you separate liver edge from spleen edge?
viva.a: The spleen carries a notch and fingers cannot pass above it toward the ribs.

viva.q: What liver size counts as massive in the book?
viva.a: Over 7 centimetres below the rib edge, seen in leukaemia or liver cancer.

viva.q: What spleen size counts as moderate?
viva.a: From 2 to 7 centimetres, classically with portal hypertension.

viva.q: Why bend the knees before feeling?
viva.a: It slackens the belly wall so deeper lumps and soreness are felt.

title.en: Percussion, liver length and belly fluid

items.summary: Tapping the liver span against age norms, testing for free fluid in the belly, and grading any fluid found.

blocks.title: Liver length
bullets: Mark the top of the liver at the right fifth rib gap and measure its span in centimetres.
Compare with the book norms: under 1 year 4 to 5, 1 to 5 years 6 to 7, and 5 to 12 years 8 to 9 centimetres.

head: Test
What it means
rows: Dullness when the kidney area is swollen

head: Grade
Meaning
rows: Puddle test positive, fluid seen only on scan
Shifting dullness present with no fluid wave
Fluid wave present with a tense belly

viva.q: What liver span fits a 3 year old?
viva.a: About 6 to 7 centimetres by the book norms for 1 to 5 years.

viva.q: Which test finds the smallest fluid?
viva.a: The puddle test, which catches under 150 millilitres.
Shifting dullness present with no fluid wave felt.

items.summary: Patient listening for gut gurgles on both sides of the navel, then hunting for bruits and vein hums and what each hints at.

blocks.title: Gut sounds
bullets: Listen on the right and left of the navel for up to 3 minutes before calling them absent.
Note whether gurgles sound normal, increased, reduced or missing.

blocks.title: Bruits and hums
bullets: A hum over the liver hints at a liver cancer.
A hum over the spleen hints at a vessel tumour.
A hum along an artery hints at a bulge in its wall.
A hum near the kidney hints at narrowing of its artery.
A vein hum hints at blockage of the portal vein.

viva.q: How long do you listen before calling gut sounds absent?
viva.a: Up to 3 minutes, on both sides of the navel.

viva.q: What does a hum over the liver suggest?
viva.a: It hints at a liver cancer with extra blood flow.

unsure: The book quotes gut sounds of 2 to 3 per minute, which seems low against standard teaching, so the figure was left out for review.

title.en: Stool, vomit and lump words that separate causes

items.summary: Everyday definitions for bleeding, diarrhoea and vomiting words, plus two classic comparisons: gut versus lung blood, and spleen versus kidney lumps.

blocks.title: Stool and urge words
bullets: Fresh red blood in the stool points to bleeding low in the gut.
Black altered blood in the stool points to bleeding high in the gut.
Loose stools beyond 14 days count as persistent diarrhoea.
Painful urge with little passage is tenesmus.

blocks.title: Vomit words
bullets: Green vomit suggests blockage high in the gut.
Sudden projectile vomit without nausea suggests high pressure inside the skull.
Blood mixed with phlegm comes from the chest, while vomited blood comes from the gut.

viva.q: How do you separate fresh red blood from black stools?
viva.a: Fresh red means low gut bleeding, black altered blood means high gut bleeding.
Blockage high in the gut below the bile entry.

viva.q: Give two signs favouring spleen over kidney.
viva.a: A felt notch and crossing the navel midline favour the spleen.
